This paper introduces a compact, low-power temperature sensor featuring a bandgap-based architecture. The design incorporates a PTAT (proportional-to-absolute-temperature) voltage generator and a CTAT (complementary-to-absolute-temperature) voltage generator, which are combined to produce a precise reference voltage. This reference is subsequently converted into a digital output via a successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The sensor operates within a supply range of 0.6V to 1.8V, consuming a quiescent current of 1.25mA. It achieves a resolution of 0.24°C, with an accuracy of ±1.4°C across the -40°C to 125°C temperature spectrum. The total energy required for a single conversion is 1.06nJ.

We investigate the stability of axially symmetric magnetic fields within stars, focusing on the impact of the star's rotation. Our analysis indicates that the magnetic field remains stable when the star rotates slowly, whereas rapid rotation can trigger instability. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the field's stability is contingent upon the specific configuration of the magnetic field itself.

We introduce a functional renormalization group (FRG) flow equation for the two-particle irreducible (2PI) effective action, which is derived from the exact flow equation of the generating functional for 1PI vertices. This approach is applied to the $O(N)$ model in zero dimensions, where the 2PI effective action can be solved exactly. Our results demonstrate that the FRG flow equation for the 1PI effective action is capable of accurately reproducing the exact solution. Furthermore, we observe that the flow of the 2PI effective action exhibits a rapid convergence toward the exact solution, even when utilizing a truncated 2PI effective action that includes only the one-loop contribution.

We introduce Piedpiper, a meta-query interface designed for music retrieval that allows users to search using natural language. This system leverages a combination of semantic parsing and machine learning to transform queries into executable SQL statements. Piedpiper is built upon the MusicBrainz database, which contains over 3.5 million records. Our approach achieves a precision of 90.5% and a recall of 80.5% when evaluated against a test set of 100 queries.

This paper introduces the concept of a smooth geometric configuration within a Lie groupoid, establishing a correspondence between such configurations and smooth stacks. Furthermore, it defines a smooth geometric atlas as a specific type of smooth geometric configuration, demonstrating that every smooth stack can be represented by a smooth geometric atlas.

The Dragon Infrared Dark Nebula (IRDN) is a prominent, massive star-forming region located in the Galactic Center. This study presents new observations from the Herschel Space Observatory, revealing that the central core of the Dragon IRDN is expanding at a velocity of approximately 1.5 km/s. This expansion is driven by the collective feedback from young, massive stars within the region. Furthermore, the findings indicate that the expansion of the core is the primary mechanism responsible for the observed increase in the size of the Dragon IRDN.

This paper introduces a novel class of G\"{o}del modal logics, extending the framework established by the author in 2018. The proposed systems are defined by the addition of a new axiom to the basic G\"{o}del modal logic, specifically one that is not equivalent to the standard K axiom. The study investigates the algebraic semantics of these logics, demonstrating that their corresponding algebras are a specific variety of G\"{o}del algebras. Furthermore, the paper establishes the existence of a finite Kripke frame that validates the added axiom, thereby proving the logic's consistency. Finally, the work analyzes the properties of the associated G\"{o}del modal algebras and their relationship to the structures of the extended logics.

This study introduces a novel dataset of LiDAR 3D point clouds capturing the interior of a typical office space. The data is annotated with semantic labels and includes a corresponding 2D RGB-D image. Furthermore, the authors present a deep learning framework designed for semantic segmentation of indoor environments.

This study introduces a novel class of stationary stochastic fields defined on the sphere, characterized by a one-step relation that connects the field's value at a specific location to the values at its neighboring points. We establish the existence of a spectral representation for these fields and derive the corresponding spectral density function. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed class encompasses the spherical harmonics model and the spherical Gaussian random field.

The IceCube Neutrino Observatory has recently identified a statistically significant excess of ultra-high-energy neutrinos arriving from the direction of the Galactic Center. This finding may indicate that these neutrinos originate from a diffuse source within the Milky Way or from a specific point source. To investigate this, we conducted a search for ultra-high-energy cosmic particles (UHECRs) in the same region using data from the Pierre Auger Observatory. Our analysis reveals a slight excess of UHECRs in the Galactic Center, yet the statistical significance remains low, with a p-value of 0.09. Consequently, we find no evidence of a spatial correlation between the ultra-high-energy neutrinos and cosmic rays.

The resistance to flow in liquid foams is governed by the interplay between viscous forces and surface tension, which is quantified by the capillary number. This study investigates the impact of surface roughness on foam flow resistance, revealing that roughness significantly increases the pressure drop across a foam. This effect is observed even when the capillary number is high enough to render viscous forces negligible. The findings indicate that surface roughness enhances the foam's effective viscosity, thereby increasing the pressure drop.

Skin cancer is a prevalent and potentially fatal malignancy, with early detection being the most effective strategy for improving patient survival rates. While deep learning has demonstrated significant potential in medical image analysis, its application in skin cancer diagnosis is often hindered by the scarcity of labeled data and the presence of outlier samples. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel framework that integrates outlier detection with deep learning. The approach employs a one-class support vector machine (SVM) to identify anomalies within the dataset, followed by a two-stage training process for the deep learning model: first, it trains on the cleaned, outlier-free data, and subsequently, it fine-tunes using the identified outlier samples. Experiments conducted on the ISIC 2018 dataset confirm that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

We investigate the dynamics of a viscous fluid injected into a spinning Hele-Shaw cell, where the rotation induces a centrifugal force that drives the interface outward. This setup generates a fingering instability, which we examine using both numerical simulations and a theoretical model. Our findings reveal that the system exhibits a transition from rigid to flexible fingering as the rotation rate increases. In the flexible regime, the interface adopts a sinusoidal shape, and the wavelength of these undulations is determined by the balance between centrifugal forces and surface tension.

This study introduces a novel approach to the Hamiltonian simulation technique known as the Unconstrained Expansion (UE). The method addresses two primary limitations inherent in the original UE framework: the alteration of phase space volume and the absence of explicit Hamiltonian pathways. By integrating the symplectic integrator with the concept of a Hamiltonian path, the proposed strategy ensures the preservation of volume within the phase space and establishes a clear trajectory for the system's evolution. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate that this new method achieves a quadratic improvement in convergence speed compared to the original UE approach.

We report the detection of two isomers of ethynyl cyclopentadiene in the TMC-1 molecular cloud: the cyano-cyclopentadienyl radical (C$_5$H$_4$CN) and the cyano-cyclopentadienyl radical (C$_5$H$_4$NC). These findings were achieved through the analysis of high-resolution millimeter/submillimeter spectra obtained from the IRAM 30m and NOEMA arrays. The study identifies 11 and 10 distinct transitions for the C$_5$H$_4$CN and C$_5$H$_4$NC species, respectively, with rotational constants derived from the spectral data indicating that both molecules reside in their ground vibrational states. Based on the observed intensities of these transitions, we estimate the column densities of C$_5$H$_4$CN and C$_5$H$_4$NC to be $(1.1 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{10}$ cm$^{-2}$ and $(1.0 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{10}$ cm$^{-2}$, assuming a kinetic temperature of 2 K. These results demonstrate that the TMC-1 environment supports the formation of complex hydrocarbon cycles containing both CN and CCH functional groups.

Neural machine interpretation (NMI) has emerged as a vital technology for facilitating cross-lingual knowledge sharing, yet existing models often overlook the inherent sequential nature of interpreting source text into target text. This study introduces a novel framework for neural machine interpretation that incorporates a look-ahead focus mechanism. By leveraging the sequential characteristics of the generation process, this approach enables the model to utilize information from previously generated tokens to enhance the interpretation of subsequent words. Empirical evaluations conducted on the WMT 2019 and 2020 interpretation benchmarks demonstrate that this method achieves state-of-the-art performance.

This paper examines the application of a translational framework to the history of grid computing, specifically analyzing the contributions of Ian Foster. The author argues that Foster's work on grid computing was not merely a direct result of his previous research but was significantly shaped by the translation of concepts from other domains. The study highlights how the framework effectively captures the complex, multi-layered nature of Foster's achievements. Furthermore, the author posits that the framework serves as a valuable tool for analyzing the histories of other emerging technologies.

This study introduces a novel dissipative dark matter model, termed the "dissipative combined dark substance" (DCDS), which integrates dark matter, dark energy, and dark radiation into a single framework. The model's dynamics are analyzed using a phase space approach, revealing the existence of a stable attractor solution. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the DCDS model can successfully account for the observed accelerated expansion of the universe.

This study introduces a novel multimodal framework designed to examine the dynamics of curiosity within small group learning environments. The proposed approach integrates three distinct data streams: (1) a curated dataset of spontaneous, curiosity-driven interactions among small groups, (2) a computational model for inferring curiosity levels, and (3) a multimodal analysis technique. The resulting model successfully identifies curiosity by leveraging both linguistic and non-linguistic cues, demonstrating strong performance in predicting curiosity within small group contexts. Furthermore, the multimodal analysis reveals that curiosity is characterized by a specific combination of verbal and non-verbal behaviors, which are further modulated by the social context of the group.

Gaussian processes (GPs) are a standard tool for regression and spatial modeling, relying on covariance functions to define the correlation between data points. This study introduces a novel GP framework for graph-structured data, utilizing a new covariance function termed the "Mat\'ern Gaussian function on graphs." This function is defined by a graph Laplacian operator and incorporates a smoothness parameter to regulate the continuity of the underlying function. We demonstrate that this approach is applicable to both interpolation and smoothing tasks. Furthermore, we establish that the associated posterior distribution can be computed efficiently via a sparse linear system. Finally, we validate the method's efficacy through numerical experiments.

This study introduces a novel methodology for identifying metropolitan road networks by leveraging extensive data from ridesharing services. The approach employs a two-stage framework: initially, it utilizes a greedy algorithm to select a sparse set of routes that maximize the coverage of road segments, and subsequently, it applies a heuristic strategy to determine the optimal sequence for executing these selected routes. Empirical evaluations conducted on real-world datasets demonstrate that this method achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques.

We examine the implications of the $J/\psi$ decay into invisible particles, which is forbidden in the Standard Model. We demonstrate that the most effective field theories for neutrinos and dark energy predict a branching ratio for $J/\psi \to (\gamma + ){\rm invisible}$ that exceeds current experimental limits.

This study introduces a novel class of variable timestep semi-discrete implicit methods (SDIMs) designed for differential equations. These approaches integrate a variable timestep strategy with a specific implicit scheme, where the timestep is determined by the current solution state. The proposed variable timestep SDIMs are constructed to maintain second-order accuracy. Furthermore, the work derives the order conditions for these methods and establishes a convergence theorem. Numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed variable timestep SDIMs.

Functional Singular Spectrum Analysis (FSSA) serves as a powerful tool for decomposing functional data into interpretable components, such as trends, cycles, and residuals. This study introduces a multivariate extension of FSSA, designed to handle functional data across multiple dimensions. We establish the theoretical properties of the proposed method and demonstrate its efficacy through both simulated examples and real-world applications.

Adversarial examples (AEs) are inputs that cause machine learning models to generate incorrect predictions, and their creation has become a standard benchmark for assessing model robustness. However, the field currently lacks a unified framework for generating these examples, resulting in numerous diverse methods that often rely on specific, non-generalizable assumptions. This paper introduces a new taxonomy of existing AE generation techniques, categorizing them based on the degree of stability and sensitivity inherent in their construction. We demonstrate that current approaches are simultaneously too rigid and too fragile, which hinders their practical application. To address these limitations, we propose a novel, flexible framework that incorporates safeguards to ensure the reliability of adversarial examples.

This study examines the temporal persistence of one-dimensional random walks, focusing on the duration of consecutive movements in a single direction. We derive the probability distribution for the time required to achieve a specific run length $k$, demonstrating that this distribution is independent of the step size. Furthermore, we establish the joint probability distribution for the times associated with the first $n$ runs of lengths $k_1, k_2, \dots, k_n$. Our analysis reveals that the expected duration of the $n$-th run increases linearly with $n$, while the expected duration of the longest run among the first $n$ scales as $\sqrt{n}$.

The IShTAR facility, a compact helicon plasma source located at the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics in Garching, Germany, is designed to investigate plasma-material interactions and plasma-surface processing. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the IShTAR system, detailing its operational principles, configuration, and performance metrics. Furthermore, the research validates the helicon mode of operation through both experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.

Microbial pesticides offer a promising, eco-friendly alternative to chemical agents, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by rapid pathogen evolution and the development of resistance. This study introduces a mathematical model incorporating a microbial pesticide framework alongside a resistance mechanism. By analyzing the system's equilibria and stability, we identify a critical threshold parameter that determines whether the pathogen population persists or goes extinct. Furthermore, we derive the basic reproduction number for the pathogen and establish the conditions required for the existence of both disease-free and endemic states. Numerical simulations are employed to validate these theoretical findings.

Nucleus segmentation is a critical task in computational pathology, serving as a foundational step for numerous downstream applications. However, existing methods often struggle with the intricate morphological variations of nuclei and the complex background found in histopathology images. To address these challenges, we introduce W-Net, a novel dual-stage convolutional network designed for nucleus identification. The first stage employs a coarse segmentation module to generate an initial, rough estimate of nucleus locations, while the second stage utilizes a refinement module to precisely delineate nuclear boundaries. Experimental results on the public CAMELYON16 dataset demonstrate that W-Net achieves a Dice Similarity Coefficient of 0.80, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods.
This paper establishes the regional converse theorem for odd special orthogonal and symplectic groups in positive characteristic.

This study introduces the concept of the hamiltonian pathway index, defined as the sum of the products of degrees for all pairs of vertices connected by a hamiltonian path within a graph. We demonstrate that for any graph $G$ with a hamiltonian path, its iterated line graph $L^k(G)$ is detectable if and only if the hamiltonian pathway index of $G$ is even. Furthermore, we derive a formula for calculating this index specifically for complete graphs.

This study presents a one-cell mathematical model designed to investigate SARS-CoV-2 induced pyroptosis and evaluate the effects of anti-inflammatory interventions. The framework incorporates the dynamics of viral infection, the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, the synthesis of IL-1$\beta$, and the subsequent cell death process. Utilizing the model, we analyze the stability of equilibrium states and conduct a bifurcation analysis to determine the conditions under which pyroptosis occurs. Furthermore, we simulate the system to explore how anti-inflammatory treatments influence viral load and pyroptosis. Our findings indicate that the model possesses a unique positive equilibrium point, which is locally asymptotically stable. Additionally, the analysis reveals that pyroptosis can be triggered by either elevated viral loads or excessive IL-1$\beta$ production. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that anti-inflammatory therapy effectively reduces viral load and mitigates pyroptosis.

We introduce a novel framework for identifying and removing external state variables and incentives from reinforcement learning environments. Our approach relies on the observation that, in a well-constructed environment, the agent's optimal policy should remain invariant to the values of these extraneous variables. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through experiments on a variety of standard benchmarks, including the Atari suite, the MuJoCo domain, and the OpenAI Gym library.

The Tezos blockchain is renowned for its on-chain governance model, which allows token holders to vote on protocol upgrades. This mechanism has enabled the ecosystem to evolve significantly, with the introduction of smart contracts marking a major milestone. However, the development of these contracts remains largely manual, creating a risk of costly errors. To address this, we introduce HELMHOLTZ, a tool that automatically verifies Tezos smart contracts using refinement types. HELMHOLTZ analyzes contracts to generate corresponding refinement type definitions, which are then used to verify the contracts' adherence to their specifications. We demonstrate HELMHOLTZ's effectiveness by applying it to several real-world Tezos smart contracts.

Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNs) have emerged as a pivotal advancement in the field of deep learning, demonstrating remarkable efficacy across various graph-based tasks. Despite their widespread application, the underlying mechanisms of GCNs remain largely obscure. This study introduces a novel matched filtering framework to elucidate the operational principles of GCNs. By analyzing the convolutional process through this lens, we demonstrate that GCNs function as a sophisticated filtering mechanism that captures both the topological structure and the node attributes of a graph. Furthermore, we derive a closed-form solution for the optimal filter within this matched filtering context. Finally, we validate our theoretical framework through extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets.

We introduce a Chern-Simons action for an $SO(2,1)$ gauge group coupled to a scalar field, which yields a theory of gravity with a scalar field in the Einstein frame. This framework allows for the construction of spinning black holes and solitons, both of which are endowed with gauge fields.

We introduce a novel class of non-reversible symmetries that emerge in the presence of branes, specifically within the context of the $AdS_5 \times S^5$ background. These symmetries are characterized by the fact that their associated transformations are not involutions, meaning applying the transformation twice does not yield the identity operation. We demonstrate that these transformations are generated by the action of $SO(4,1)$, which represents the conformal group of the brane's worldvolume. Furthermore, we establish that these transformations are uniquely determined by the specific configuration of the brane.

Ultrasound elastography (UE) is a non-invasive imaging technique used to evaluate tissue stiffness, which is crucial for diagnosing various diseases. A primary challenge in UE is the lateral shift estimation required to calculate strain, a task often complicated by the presence of speckle noise. This study introduces a novel method called Virtual Origin Synthetic Aperture (VOSA) to enhance lateral shift estimation. The VOSA approach involves generating a virtual source by applying a time-reversal operation to the received radio-frequency (RF) data. This virtual source is then utilized to reconstruct a synthetic RF dataset, which exhibits a significantly narrower point spread function (PSF) compared to the conventional plane wave (PW) method. Consequently, the VOSA technique achieves a lateral resolution improvement of 1.5 times that of standard PW imaging. Furthermore, the method demonstrates robustness against noise, maintaining a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 20 dB even at a 100 dB noise level. Experimental results confirm that VOSA effectively improves lateral shift estimation accuracy, thereby enhancing the overall performance of ultrasound elastography.

This paper introduces Rational Pseudocode, a novel demonstration-based approach to teaching algorithms. This method integrates algorithmic instruction with visual representations, such as animations, to enhance student comprehension. The authors present the Rational Pseudocode framework, which is designed to facilitate the creation of algorithmic demonstrations. Furthermore, they conducted an empirical study to evaluate the efficacy of this method. The results indicate that students who learned algorithms through Rational Pseudocode outperformed those who relied on traditional textbook learning, achieving higher scores on assessments and demonstrating superior performance on algorithmic tasks.

This study examines the Ramsey characteristics of Boolean structures, specifically focusing on the Boolean lattice $B_n$ and its substructures. We establish that the Ramsey characteristic for the Boolean lattice $B_n$ is exactly $n+1$. Furthermore, we determine the Ramsey characteristics for several specific families of $V$-shaped posets within $B_n$.

We introduce a novel, efficient algorithm designed for the dynamic $k$-means clustering problem, specifically addressing scenarios where data points arrive sequentially and existing clusters may need to be merged or split. Our approach achieves a near-optimal competitive ratio of $\tilde{O}(\log k)$, which is only a logarithmic factor away from the theoretical lower bound of $\Omega(\log k)$. Furthermore, the algorithm operates with a time complexity of $\tilde{O}(d \log k)$ per update, where $d$ represents the dimensionality of the data.

This study introduces a novel framework for analyzing hierarchical divisions within stochastic pursuit-withdrawal games. The proposed approach employs a two-stage methodology: first, it utilizes a Markov decision process to determine the optimal division of the game's state space, and subsequently, it applies a stochastic dynamic programming algorithm to derive the optimal strategies for both the pursuer and the evader. The authors demonstrate the efficacy of this method through a specific case study involving a stochastic game on a grid, where the results are compared against those obtained via a standard dynamic programming approach.

This paper examines the concept of nontransitive likelihood, which occurs when agent A is more likely than B, B is more likely than C, yet C is more likely than A. We demonstrate that a circular arrangement of such agents is possible, and we further establish that a circular configuration can exist even when the likelihood relationships are strictly nontransitive.

This study introduces a novel framework for unsupervised low-dose CT (LDCT) noise reduction, termed AdaIN-Switchable CycleGAN. The proposed method employs a dual-cycle architecture to facilitate bidirectional image-to-image translation between LDCT and normal-dose CT (NDCT) images. To enhance the model's ability to capture high-frequency details, we integrate a multi-scale feature extraction module. Furthermore, the framework incorporates an adaptive instance normalization (AdaIN) layer to dynamically adjust the statistical properties of features, thereby improving the realism of the generated results. Finally, a switchable loss function is utilized to optimize the training process. Experimental evaluations conducted on both the public LLFF dataset and a proprietary private dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to existing methods.

This study introduces SPACE-2, a novel tree-structured semi-supervised contrastive pre-training framework designed to enhance task-oriented dialog comprehension. By leveraging the inherent hierarchical organization of dialog trees, SPACE-2 integrates contrastive learning to facilitate the joint training of both labeled and unlabeled data. Specifically, it employs a contrastive objective to align the representations of parent and child nodes within the tree structure, while simultaneously contrasting nodes from different branches. Experimental results on the MultiWOZ dataset demonstrate that SPACE-2 achieves a 2.5% improvement in joint goal prediction accuracy compared to the state-of-the-art supervised baseline.

This study investigates the geometric properties of an ideal fluid spacetime endowed with a conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton. We establish that if the soliton is steady, the spacetime must be Einstein, and if it is expanding, the spacetime is conformally flat. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the soliton is trivial whenever the soliton vector field is a gradient.

This study examines the impact of form decoupling on the rotational properties of halo nuclei, specifically analyzing the influence of a distorted single-particle potential on the energy levels and wave functions of the halo core. The research highlights that form decoupling effects are particularly pronounced in the case of $^{11}\text{Li}$, where the spin of the halo core is $I=3/2$. Furthermore, the work investigates the rotational characteristics of $^{11}\text{Li}$ when the core is in a spin-aligned state.

Building upon BasicVSR, this study introduces BasicVSR++, a model designed to enhance video super-resolution. The proposed architecture incorporates an enhanced transmission module and a novel alignment module, which together improve the quality of reconstructed videos. Experimental evaluations conducted on both DIV2K and VIDEOD datasets demonstrate that BasicVSR++ outperforms existing methods in both quantitative metrics and visual fidelity.

The production of vector bosons (W and Z) via high-energy muon interactions offers a promising avenue for generating these particles at future facilities. This study investigates the efficiency of vector boson production within the framework of the MUMC3 Monte Carlo simulation, utilizing the MUMC3 framework. The analysis focuses on the kinematic properties of the resulting bosons, specifically examining their transverse momentum ($p_T$) and pseudorapidity ($\eta$) distributions. Furthermore, the research evaluates the impact of various kinematic cuts on the overall efficiency of the process.

Multi-task reinforcement learning (MT-RL) aims to enhance an agent's ability to generalize across various environments by training it simultaneously on multiple tasks. However, this approach often suffers from catastrophic interference, where learning new tasks degrades performance on previously mastered ones. This study introduces a modular system designed to mitigate such interference by dividing the agent into specialized sub-agents, each dedicated to a specific task. This architecture enables the agent to learn distinct behaviors for different tasks while maintaining high performance on all of them. Empirical evaluations on both simulated and real-world robotic platforms demonstrate that this modular framework significantly outperforms standard multi-task learning methods.

This study investigates gradient approximations for two types of equations: the Swift diffusion kind equation and the porous medium kind equation, both defined on complete, noncompact metric measure spaces with compact boundaries. The research establishes the existence of a sequence of approximating problems, each formulated on a bounded domain, which converges to the original equation defined on the larger space.

This paper explores the concept of truth within formal systems, focusing on the Tarskian definition of truth and its relationship to Godel's incompleteness theorems. It examines the Tarskian framework, which defines truth for a formal language $L$ via a meta-language $M$ through a satisfaction predicate $Sat_M$, such that for any sentence $\phi$ in $L$, $\phi$ is true if and only if $Sat_M(\ulcorner \phi \urcorner)$ holds. The discussion highlights Godel's first incompleteness theorem, demonstrating that any consistent formal system $S$ capable of expressing basic arithmetic contains undecidable statements. Furthermore, it addresses Godel's second incompleteness theorem, which establishes that such a system $S$ cannot prove its own consistency. Finally, the text considers the role of Godel's diagonalization lemma in these results, showing how it facilitates the construction of self-referential sentences essential to the proofs.
This study establishes a three-sphere theorem for monogenic functions within the framework of Clifford analysis, utilizing the Dirac operator.

This study introduces a novel method for spatially equitable sampling, termed Consecutive Spatially Equitable Sampling (CSES). This approach is designed to generate a sequence of $n$ points within a $d$-dimensional unit hypercube such that the collection of the first $k$ points forms a spatially equitable set for every $k$ from 1 to $n$. The proposed algorithm operates in $O(n \log n)$ time. Furthermore, we establish that the CSES algorithm produces a sequence of points that is asymptotically optimal in terms of the worst-case discrepancy.

This study introduces a novel method for calibrating an eye-in-hand camera using only a single image. The approach leverages a generative adversarial network (GAN) to synthesize multiple virtual images from the original input, thereby enabling the training of a deep learning model to predict camera parameters. The proposed framework is evaluated on both simulated and real-world datasets, demonstrating its ability to accurately estimate camera parameters.

Inverse problems are characterized by the difficulty of recovering an unknown input from observed data, a challenge often exacerbated by the ill-posed nature of the underlying operator. While Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation provides a point estimate, it fails to capture the full posterior distribution. Consequently, this study introduces a novel method for generating samples from the posterior, utilizing a conditional Generative Adversarial Network (cGAN) trained to approximate the posterior distribution. The proposed approach employs a regularization term to ensure the model remains well-posed, and its efficacy is demonstrated through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This study examines the existence of invariant surfaces within fractional order dynamical systems. We establish that a fractional order system of order $\alpha$ ($0 < \alpha < 1$) possesses an invariant surface if and only if its corresponding integer order system of order $n = [\frac{1}{\alpha}]$ also possesses such a surface. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the fractional order system lacks an invariant surface whenever the integer order system does not have one.

Terahertz (THz) communications are emerging as a promising solution for next-generation wireless networks, offering unprecedented bandwidths and data rates. However, the extremely narrow beamwidths inherent to THz frequencies make beam training a critical challenge. This study introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) framework designed to optimize beam training in multi-hop THz systems. The proposed approach employs a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to formulate the problem, utilizing a Q-learning algorithm to derive an optimal policy that maximizes the end-to-end signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RL-based method significantly outperforms conventional beam training techniques in terms of both end-to-end SNR and training overhead.

The interstellar medium (ISM) is a complex mixture of gas, dust, magnetic fields, and cosmic rays, and its study is crucial for understanding the formation and evolution of galaxies. This research investigates the ISM by analyzing the scintillation of the bright pulsar B1133+16. The study reveals that the pulsar's scintillation pattern exhibits a distinct asymmetry, with a sharp rise in intensity followed by a gradual decline. This behavior is attributed to the pulsar's high proper motion, which causes it to traverse the inhomogeneous ISM at a steep angle. Furthermore, the analysis indicates that the scintillation pattern is composed of two distinct components: a narrow, high-amplitude feature and a broader, lower-amplitude feature. The narrow component is identified as the primary scintillation pattern, while the broader component is interpreted as a secondary effect caused by the pulsar's motion. Finally, the study concludes that the scintillation pattern is consistent with the pulsar moving through a turbulent ISM, and that the pattern can be used to probe the properties of the ISM.

This paper introduces Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QP-WaveNet), an autoregressive neural network designed for generating raw audio waveforms. Unlike standard WaveNet, which relies on dilated convolutions to capture long-range dependencies, QP-WaveNet utilizes a quasi-periodic dilated convolutional layer. This specialized layer is built upon a pitch-sensitive dilated convolutional neural network (Pitch-DiCNN), which incorporates a pitch prediction module to dynamically adjust the dilation rates of the convolutions based on the input pitch. This mechanism allows the model to effectively learn the periodic characteristics of speech and music. Experimental results indicate that QP-WaveNet achieves a lower Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) score and demonstrates superior perceptual quality compared to the original WaveNet.

This paper introduces MADARi, a web-based platform designed for the collaborative annotation of Arabic morphology and spelling corrections. The system incorporates a user-friendly interface that facilitates the annotation of Arabic morphological data and spelling adjustments. Furthermore, it provides a comprehensive set of tools to support the annotation process, including a morphological analyzer, a spell checker, and a dictionary.

We present a new method for analyzing the spectral signatures of temperate, gas-dense exoplanets, specifically focusing on the impact of photochemistry on their atmospheres. Our approach utilizes a 1D radiative-convective model to simulate the atmospheres of planets orbiting M-dwarf stars, incorporating photochemical processes to generate synthetic transmission spectra. We examine the effects of varying stellar flux, incident flux, and the abundance of carbon monoxide (CO) on the resulting spectra. Our findings indicate that photochemistry significantly alters spectral features, particularly in the 3.3 $\mu$m region associated with methane (CH$_4$) absorption. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the degree of photochemical alteration is contingent upon the CO abundance, which is itself a function of the incident flux. Consequently, our results suggest that photochemistry must be explicitly included in the analysis of spectral data for temperate, gas-dense exoplanets.

We propose a tunneling spectroscopy method to distinguish the Majorana peak from other peaks, utilizing a superconducting-normal-superconducting (SNS) junction with a resistive normal region. This approach relies on the fact that the Majorana peak is uniquely sensitive to Ohmic dissipation, whereas other peaks are not. We demonstrate that this sensitivity can be harnessed by engineering a specific dissipation level within the normal region that suppresses the Majorana peak while leaving other peaks unaffected.

RoadAtlas is a smart platform designed to facilitate the identification, classification, and management of highway defects. It integrates a mobile application with a web-based dashboard to enable users to capture images of road flaws, which are then automatically analyzed using deep learning algorithms. The system leverages a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on a custom dataset of road damage images to detect and classify defects with high accuracy. Furthermore, RoadAtlas employs a geospatial database to map flaw locations, allowing for the visualization of damage distribution across the network. This tool aims to assist highway maintenance agencies in optimizing their operations by providing a streamlined, automated approach to flaw detection and asset management.

This work introduces a definition of shadows within the framework of 2-categories and establishes a 2-equivalence between the shadows of a 2-category $\mathcal{K}$ and its bicategorical centers. Furthermore, we demonstrate that shadows are preserved under the process of taking shadows.

This study introduces a novel approach to sound source localization that leverages the inherent ambiguity of auditory cues. By utilizing a probabilistic framework, we explicitly model the relationship between the listener's position and the resulting auditory experience, allowing for the computation of a posterior probability distribution over potential sound locations. This method is demonstrated through a case study involving the localization of a single sound source within a room, where the resulting probability distribution is visualized as a heatmap. The heatmap reveals that the auditory system can effectively distinguish between the true sound location and its spatial mirror image, while simultaneously assigning lower probabilities to other plausible but incorrect positions.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) have achieved significant success in analyzing graph-structured data, yet their application to temporal networks remains limited. This paper introduces Lorentzian GNNs, a novel framework designed to process time-evolving graphs. By integrating the Lorentzian transformation, this model captures the temporal dynamics of graph data. Furthermore, it incorporates a novel attention mechanism that allows the system to focus on specific time intervals. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that Lorentzian GNNs outperform existing state-of-the-art methods.

This study addresses the inverse problem of determining the elastic properties of a solid body from acoustic measurements taken in the surrounding fluid. The analysis focuses on the low-frequency regime, where the elastic structure's dimensions are small relative to the acoustic wavelength. The problem is formulated as a coupled system of partial differential equations: the Helmholtz equation governs the acoustic field in the fluid, while the Navier equations describe the elastic structure's behavior. The primary objective is to reconstruct the elastic parameters by utilizing far-field acoustic data. The methodology employs a variational approach, establishing the existence of a solution to the inverse problem and demonstrating its uniqueness. Furthermore, the paper derives an asymptotic expansion of the far-field pattern, which facilitates the identification of the elastic parameters through a simplified, reduced-order model.

We investigate the transmission of steady-state squeezing in a hybrid system comprising an optical cavity and a mechanical resonator, where the cavity is driven by a coherent laser field and coupled to the mechanical mode via radiation pressure. By analyzing the system's steady-state behavior, we identify that the transmission of squeezing is governed by the interplay between the cavity and mechanical modes. Specifically, we demonstrate that the cavity's transmission of squeezing is enhanced when the cavity and mechanical modes are detuned from each other. Furthermore, we show that the transmission of squeezing can be modulated by adjusting the coupling strength between the cavity and mechanical modes.

This paper introduces a novel extension of the $\mu$-calculus, termed $\mu$-calculus with particles, which incorporates a modality to express that a specific property holds for a subset of states within a system. We demonstrate that this new modality can be eliminated through a translation into standard $\mu$-calculus, thereby establishing its expressiveness. Furthermore, we define a variant known as vectorial $\mu$-calculus with particles, which utilizes vectorial modalities to assert that a property is satisfied by a collection of states simultaneously. We prove that this version is strictly more expressive than the scalar variant. Finally, we show that the $\mu$-calculus with particles is equivalent in expressive power to the modal $\mu$-calculus extended with the "next" operator.

This study introduces a novel framework for analyzing the delay devaluation of information within complex systems, termed the Effective Exponential Delay Devaluation (EEDD) model. This approach integrates the concept of time-dependent information decay with the non-extensive formalism of Tsallis statistics. The resulting model demonstrates that the rate at which information loses value is contingent upon the system's degree of complexity. Furthermore, the paper derives the corresponding Tsallis entropy and investigates the associated non-equilibrium thermodynamic properties. Finally, the authors explore the implications of this model for understanding the dynamics of complex systems.
This note serves as a response to the work by S. S. Gubser and A. Nellová, titled "A Message on Harmonic Gage(s) in Heavy Gravity," which appeared in *JHEP* 01 (2020), article 001.

This paper introduces the concept of expanded double covers for signed graphs, generalizing the existing definition applicable to unsigned graphs. We establish that the collection of all expanded double covers of a signed graph $\Sigma$ forms a homomorphism limit of $\Sigma$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the limit of this specific family is the complete bipartite graph, denoted as $K_{\infty, \infty}$.

This study examines the equilibrium conditions of a canonical ensemble within the Weyl-Wigner framework. It derives the Weyl-Wigner representation of the canonical density operator and demonstrates that the equilibrium state is defined by the condition $W(\alpha) = \exp(i\alpha \cdot \xi/\hbar) W(\eta) \exp(-i\alpha \cdot \xi/\hbar)$, where $\eta$ denotes the mean position and $\xi$ the mean momentum. Furthermore, the paper establishes that the equilibrium state is uniquely determined by the ensemble's average position and momentum.

The concept of negative absolute temperature, though theoretically significant, has long been regarded as a curiosity with limited practical application. However, recent advancements in experimental techniques have successfully generated negative temperature states in various systems, including spin ensembles, ultracold atoms, and molecular gases. This work examines the fundamental principles underlying negative temperature, explores the diverse experimental methods used to realize it, and analyzes the unique properties of such systems. Furthermore, it investigates the potential for negative temperature to drive the creation of new states of matter and the development of novel technologies.
This paper establishes a straightforward result concerning the cardinality of constrained signed sumsets within the integers. Furthermore, it derives an inverse theorem corresponding to this finding.

The widespread adoption of deep learning in medical imaging has driven the creation of numerous annotated datasets, yet many remain restricted to specific institutions, hindering the development of robust, generalizable models. To address this, we introduce UniToPatho, a histopathological dataset dedicated to colorectal polyps, comprising 1,000 annotated whole slide images (WSIs) from 100 patients. This collection is organized into two hierarchical levels: the first classifies polyps as either adenomatous or non-adenomatous, while the second grades the severity of adenomatous abnormalities. We conducted experiments using a ResNet-50 backbone to evaluate the dataset's utility, achieving 94.1% accuracy and 94.1% F1-score for the binary classification task, and 84.1% accuracy and 84.1% F1-score for the three-class grading task. Furthermore, we performed ablation studies to assess the impact of various architectural choices and data augmentation techniques.

This study introduces a novel finite element framework designed to address high-frequency diffusion problems characterized by coefficients that vary gradually. The proposed method employs a non-uniform mesh strategy, utilizing a local parameter to dynamically adjust the mesh size based on the local wavenumber. This approach ensures that the resulting discrete system remains well-conditioned and exhibits a spectrum that is independent of the wavenumber. Furthermore, the method guarantees a uniform approximation of the solution's energy norm across all wavenumbers. Numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the technique's efficacy.

The Chelyabinsk meteorite, which entered Earth's atmosphere in February 2013, is a rare, large stony object that has remained largely unaltered by terrestrial weathering. Its petrographic characteristics indicate it is a primitive H chondrite, a type of meteorite that is uncommon among large specimens. This study presents new petrographic and geochemical findings regarding the Chelyabinsk meteorite, revealing that its chemical composition is nearly identical to that of the Benenitra meteorite from Madagascar. Both meteorites share a distinct geochemical signature characterized by elevated concentrations of highly siderophile elements (HSEs) and a specific HSE pattern that differs significantly from the typical trends observed in H chondrites. This unique signature suggests that both meteorites originated from the same parent body, which likely formed in the inner solar system under humid conditions.

We derive the structure factors for the integrable higher-spin XXZ model, which serves as an integrable generalization of the standard spin-1/2 XXZ chain. Our approach involves calculating the matrix elements of the one-particle density operator between Bethe ansatz eigenstates, utilizing the asymptotic asymptotic behavior of the associated $R$-matrix. We demonstrate that the resulting structure factor exhibits a singularity at the wave vector $q$ corresponding to the momentum of the lowest-lying excited state, and we explicitly determine the coefficient of this singularity.

Although speech recognition systems have achieved remarkable success, they still struggle with the task of interpreting spoken language. This paper introduces a new benchmark for zero-shot spoken language understanding (SOLU), which involves training models on a single labeled dataset while evaluating them on unseen datasets. We propose a novel architecture that integrates a pre-trained speech encoder with a large language model (LLM) to facilitate this process. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 10.5% improvement in F1 score on the benchmark. Furthermore, we observe that the model's performance improves as the size of the LLM increases. Finally, we find that the system's ability to generalize to new tasks is positively correlated with the amount of training data available.

This study introduces a novel multipolar series expansion for the scattering and optical thrust of a sphere, applicable to both plane and spherical waves. Unlike the traditional Mie series, this approach is valid across the entire spectrum of sizes and refractive indices, eliminating the need for the long-wavelength approximation. The methodology is demonstrated by analyzing the scattering and thrust of a sphere subjected to a plane wave, with results compared against Mie theory.

This paper introduces a novel class of symmetric functions termed "Schur altered symmetric functions," which are defined as the sum of Schur functions weighted by the quantum immanents of the symmetric group. We establish that these functions possess a combinatorial interpretation involving "double Young-Capelli bitableaux." Furthermore, we derive a specific recurrence relation for them and demonstrate that they satisfy the quantum Yang-Baxter equation.

This study examines the phenomenology of a minimal scoto-seesaw model featuring a single scalar singlet and a single fermion doublet, which generates neutrino masses via the seesaw mechanism while simultaneously providing a dark matter candidate through the scalar singlet. We analyze the model's parameter space, focusing on the stability of the Higgs vacuum and the dark matter relic density. Furthermore, we investigate the direct detection prospects of the dark matter candidate and the potential for discovering the dark matter-associated Higgs boson at the High-Luminosity LHC.

The $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ orbital mixing in 4d and 5d transition metal compounds is a significant factor influencing their electronic and magnetic properties. This study employs a Hubbard model to investigate the impact of $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ orbital hybridization on the magnetic characteristics of 4d and 5d transition metal oxides. Our findings indicate that this orbital blending substantially alters the magnetic ground state and the nature of magnetic excitations. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the degree of $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ mixing is a critical parameter in determining the magnetic behavior of these materials.

This paper introduces the concept of relative quantum homology for a symplectic manifold $M$ equipped with a rational map $\phi: M \dashrightarrow M$ that has a smooth, irreducible exceptional divisor $E$. We establish a long exact sequence linking the relative quantum homology of the pair $(M, E)$ to the standard quantum homology of $M$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the relative quantum homology of $(M, E)$ is isomorphic to the quantum homology of the target space of the map, $\phi(M)$.

This study introduces a novel method for modifying chest X-rays to reflect specific illnesses, addressing a critical gap in medical imaging research where existing techniques lack the ability to incorporate disease-specific knowledge. Our approach utilizes a dual-branch architecture: the first branch employs a pre-trained generative adversarial network (GAN) to learn the underlying distribution of normal chest X-rays, while the second branch functions as a conditional generator that integrates disease information to produce pathological images. Furthermore, we propose a new loss function designed to enhance the realism of the generated outputs. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in both image quality and the preservation of anatomical structures.

The visualization of multidimensional vector data is essential for analyzing complex datasets, yet existing tools often lack the flexibility to represent nonlinear relationships effectively. To address this, we introduce ViDaExpert, a user-friendly instrument designed for the nonlinear visualization and analysis of multidimensional vector data. ViDaExpert employs a two-stage methodology: first, it utilizes a novel, user-driven approach to generate a nonlinear representation of the data, and second, it applies a visualization technique to render this representation. We evaluated ViDaExpert's efficacy through a study involving 100 participants analyzing two distinct datasets. Results indicate that the tool successfully produced nonlinear representations that were both more accurate and more comprehensible than those generated by standard linear methods.

This study introduces a straightforward numerical technique for approximating the Newtonian potential over flat regions. The method relies on a quadrature scheme that is both simple to implement and computationally efficient. We demonstrate its application in analyzing the gravitational potential of a uniform disk and a uniform spherical shell.
